Why scarcity forces every individual and society to make choices and tradeoffs
The four factors of production: land, labor, capital, entrepreneurship (and that money is not a factor)
Scarcity is permanent and universal; a shortage is a temporary market condition
Even 'free' goods and time involve scarcity
Scarcity as the reason economics exists

claims.claim: Scarcity is the condition in which limited resources cannot satisfy unlimited or competing human wants, and economics is the study of how people make decisions in the face of scarcity.

Resources exist in limited supply while human wants are effectively unlimited, so the goods and services that can be produced are also limited; this gap is why scarcity is a problem and why economics exists.
The factors of production are the economy's productive resources, divided into four categories: land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship.

Land is any natural resource used in production (including water, oil, minerals, forests) and earns rent; labor is human physical and mental effort and earns wages; capital is the tools, machines, and buildings used to produce goods and earns interest; entrepreneurship combines the other factors to produce output and earns profit.
Money is not a factor of production; it is used to buy the real productive resources rather than being a productive resource itself.

A shortage (excess demand) is a temporary market condition that occurs when the price is below equilibrium, so quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied; the price then rises toward equilibrium, distinguishing a shortage from permanent scarcity.
Time is often described as the ultimate scarce resource, illustrating that scarcity applies even to things with no market price.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Some introductory sources list only three classical factors (land, labor, capital), while others include entrepreneurship as a fourth.
positions: Classical political economy grouped resources as land, labor, and capital.
Modern intro-economics teaching, including Federal Reserve Education materials, adds entrepreneurship as a distinct fourth factor with profit as its return.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson uses the four-factor framing (land, labor, capital, entrepreneurship) standard in current U.S. intro-economics teaching and in the Federal Reserve Education source, and notes each factor's characteristic payment.
